doc.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019

title: Not overplaying: teamwork on the bandstand
summary: Rowe recalls Piltzecker's morning demonstration of a rude accompanist; Piltzecker talks about teamwork, texture and judiciousness.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: It does. And you demonstrated this morning quite well I thought, something not to do on the bandstand when you said, “Here’s a rude accompanist.”
It scares me that I demonstrated being rude so well I guess.
Well the students needed to see what you were talking about, and I thought you made it clear, overplaying and like, “Keep the spotlight on me” not over there.

I think everybody aspires to the best kind of teamwork possible to come up with you know, and sometimes it’s hard to just focus on what the total picture is. What is the band creating for the audience and you just contribute one part of that fabric. But yes, not overplaying and having a sense of the texture as it’s unfolding. You don’t have to play that chord or that note or this extra something necessarily because you can. And you know I can’t say that I do it all the time but I can say that I aspire to doing it all the time, you know, to being judicious and to go make that perfect solo that never happens you know.
